en.greeting: Hi! Today we'll learn words for jobs, hobbies and the weekend, so you can talk about your work and your free time. Let's go step by step.

steps.title: What do you do?
steps.text: When people meet, they often ask: **What do you do?** It's a fixed question that means 'What's your job?' (not 'what are you doing now?').
steps.body: Answer with **I'm a** + job: **I'm a teacher.** (*I'm* = I am.) If the job starts with a vowel sound (a, e, i, o, u when you say it), use **an**: **I'm an engineer.** Indonesian says *Saya guru*, with no 'adalah' and no 'seorang', but English always needs **am** and **a/an** before one job.

steps.title: Where do they work?
steps.text: Now let's add the place. Look at the verb after the job.
steps.body: Most workplaces use **work in**: in a hospital, in a shop, in an office. A farm is different: **work on a farm**. There's no real rule here, just remember it. With he/she (one person), add **-s** to the doing word: she **works**.

examples.en: My mother is a nurse. She works in a hospital.
examples.id: Ibu saya perawat. Dia bekerja di rumah sakit.

examples.en: Sari is a shop assistant. She works in a shop in Bandung.
examples.id: Sari pramuniaga. Dia bekerja di toko di Bandung.

examples.en: My uncle is an office worker. He works in an office.
examples.id: Paman saya karyawan kantor. Dia bekerja di kantor.

examples.en: Rudi is a waiter. He works in a restaurant.
examples.id: Rudi pelayan. Dia bekerja di restoran.

examples.en: Pak Made is a farmer. He works on a farm.
examples.id: Pak Made petani. Dia bekerja di ladang.

steps.title: Your turn
steps.text: Here's a man at a warung near your office.

question.prompt: Pak Joko cooks soto and nasi goreng for his customers every day. What is his job?
question.explanation: A job needs **a**: **He's a cook.** A **cooker** is a stove (kompor), not a person, and 'He's cook' has no article.

steps.title: Sports: play or go?
steps.text: Now free time! Indonesian says *main* for a lot of things, but English uses two verbs.
steps.body: Use **play** with ball sports, games and instruments: **play football**, **play chess**, **play the guitar** (instruments take **the**, sports don't). Use **go** with activities that end in **-ing**: **go swimming**, **go fishing**. Never 'play swimming'. And no **to**: *to* is for a place (go **to** the mall), and shopping is an activity, not a place, so 'go to shopping' is wrong.

steps.title: Your turn
steps.text: Sari's favourite sport happens in a pool.

question.prompt: Sari loves the water. Every Sunday morning she ___.
question.explanation: Swimming ends in **-ing**, so we use **go**, with no 'to'. Sari = she, so **go** becomes **goes** (words ending in o add **-es**, not just -s): **She goes swimming.**

steps.title: My hobby is ...
steps.text: Here's how people talk about their hobbies.
steps.body: After **My hobby is** use a verb (doing word) + **-ing**: **My hobby is reading.** Not 'My hobby is read'. Why? After *is* you need the name of an activity, and **-ing** turns *read* (membaca) into *reading* (kegiatan membaca). You can also say what you usually do: **In my free time I draw.**

examples.en: My hobby is reading.
examples.id: Hobi saya membaca.

examples.en: Rina's hobby is cooking.
examples.id: Hobi Rina memasak.

examples.en: In my free time I draw.
examples.id: Di waktu luang saya menggambar.

examples.en: Budi plays chess in his free time.
examples.id: Budi main catur di waktu luangnya.

steps.title: Build the sentence
steps.text: Your friend Dimas plays music every evening. Help him say it.

question.solution: My hobby is playing the guitar.
question.prompt: Arrange the words: Hobi saya main gitar.
question.explanation: After **My hobby is** we use **-ing**: **playing**. With an instrument, English adds **the**: **playing the guitar** (but *playing football*, with no *the*). Just remember it.

steps.title: At the weekend
steps.text: Saturday and Sunday are **the weekend**. What do people do then?
steps.body: Say **at the weekend** (British) or **on the weekend** (American): both are correct. **On Sundays**, with -s, means every Sunday. Use **go to** + a place (**go to the mall**) but **go** + -ing for an activity (**go shopping**). And we **watch** TV, we don't 'see' TV. (*Film* is British, *movie* is American.)

steps.title: Your turn
steps.text: Budi asks Rina about her weekend.

question.prompt: Budi: What do you do at the weekend? Rina: On Saturdays I ___ my friends at a café in Bandung.
question.explanation: You **meet** people: **I meet my friends.** We **play** sports and games, and **go** needs **to** before a place, not before people.

steps.title: Quick review
steps.text: Flip these cards to remember the new words.

id.greeting: Hai! Hari ini kita belajar kata-kata untuk pekerjaan, hobi dan akhir pekan, supaya kamu bisa bercerita tentang pekerjaan dan waktu luangmu. Ayo kita mulai pelan-pelan.

steps.title: What do you do?
steps.text: Saat berkenalan, orang sering bertanya: **What do you do?** Ini pertanyaan tetap yang artinya 'Apa pekerjaanmu?' (bukan 'sedang apa sekarang?').
steps.body: Jawab dengan **I'm a** + pekerjaan: **I'm a teacher.** (*I'm* = I am.) Kalau pekerjaannya diawali bunyi vokal (a, e, i, o, u waktu diucapkan), pakai **an**: **I'm an engineer.** Bahasa Indonesia bilang *Saya guru*, tanpa 'adalah' dan tanpa 'seorang', tapi bahasa Inggris selalu butuh **am** dan **a/an** sebelum satu pekerjaan.

steps.title: Di mana mereka bekerja?
steps.text: Sekarang kita tambahkan tempatnya. Perhatikan kata kerja setelah pekerjaan.
steps.body: Kebanyakan tempat kerja memakai **work in**: in a hospital, in a shop, in an office. Ladang berbeda: **work on a farm**. Tidak ada aturan khusus, hafalkan saja. Untuk he/she (satu orang), tambahkan **-s** pada kata kerjanya: she **works**.

examples.en: My mother is a nurse. She works in a hospital.
examples.id: Ibu saya perawat. Dia bekerja di rumah sakit.

examples.en: Sari is a shop assistant. She works in a shop in Bandung.
examples.id: Sari pramuniaga. Dia bekerja di toko di Bandung.

examples.en: My uncle is an office worker. He works in an office.
examples.id: Paman saya karyawan kantor. Dia bekerja di kantor.

examples.en: Rudi is a waiter. He works in a restaurant.
examples.id: Rudi pelayan. Dia bekerja di restoran.

examples.en: Pak Made is a farmer. He works on a farm.
examples.id: Pak Made petani. Dia bekerja di ladang.

steps.title: Giliranmu
steps.text: Ini bapak pemilik warung dekat kantormu.

question.prompt: Pak Joko cooks soto and nasi goreng for his customers every day. Apa pekerjaannya?
question.explanation: Pekerjaan butuh **a**: **He's a cook.** **Cooker** itu kompor, bukan orang, dan 'He's cook' tidak memakai kata sandang.

steps.title: Olahraga: play atau go?
steps.text: Sekarang waktu luang! Bahasa Indonesia bilang *main* untuk banyak hal, tapi bahasa Inggris memakai dua kata kerja.
steps.body: Pakai **play** untuk olahraga dengan bola, permainan dan alat musik: **play football**, **play chess**, **play the guitar** (alat musik pakai **the**, olahraga tidak). Pakai **go** untuk kegiatan berakhiran **-ing**: **go swimming**, **go fishing**. Jangan bilang 'play swimming'. Dan tanpa **to**: *to* untuk tempat (go **to** the mall), sedangkan shopping itu kegiatan, bukan tempat, jadi 'go to shopping' salah.

steps.title: Giliranmu
steps.text: Olahraga favorit Sari dilakukan di kolam renang.

question.prompt: Lengkapi: Sari loves the water. Every Sunday morning she ___.
question.explanation: Swimming berakhiran **-ing**, jadi pakai **go**, tanpa 'to'. Sari = she, jadi **go** berubah jadi **goes** (kata yang berakhiran o ditambah **-es**, bukan cuma -s): **She goes swimming.**

steps.title: My hobby is ...
steps.text: Begini cara orang bercerita tentang hobinya.
steps.body: Setelah **My hobby is** pakai kata kerja + **-ing**: **My hobby is reading.** Bukan 'My hobby is read'. Kenapa? Setelah *is* kamu perlu nama kegiatan, dan **-ing** mengubah *read* (membaca) jadi *reading* (kegiatan membaca). Kamu juga bisa bilang apa yang biasa kamu lakukan: **In my free time I draw.**

examples.en: My hobby is reading.
examples.id: Hobi saya membaca.

examples.en: Rina's hobby is cooking.
examples.id: Hobi Rina memasak.

examples.en: In my free time I draw.
examples.id: Di waktu luang saya menggambar.

examples.en: Budi plays chess in his free time.
examples.id: Budi main catur di waktu luangnya.

steps.title: Susun kalimatnya
steps.text: Temanmu Dimas main musik setiap malam. Bantu dia mengatakannya.

question.solution: My hobby is playing the guitar.
question.prompt: Susun kata-katanya: Hobi saya main gitar.
question.explanation: Setelah **My hobby is** kita pakai **-ing**: **playing**. Untuk alat musik, bahasa Inggris menambah **the**: **playing the guitar** (tapi *playing football*, tanpa *the*). Hafalkan saja.

steps.title: Di akhir pekan
steps.text: Sabtu dan Minggu adalah **the weekend** (akhir pekan). Apa yang orang lakukan?
steps.body: Ucapkan **at the weekend** (Inggris) atau **on the weekend** (Amerika): dua-duanya benar. **On Sundays**, pakai -s, artinya setiap hari Minggu. Pakai **go to** + tempat (**go to the mall**) tapi **go** + -ing untuk kegiatan (**go shopping**). Dan kita **watch** TV, bukan 'see' TV. (*Film* kata Inggris, *movie* kata Amerika.)

steps.title: Giliranmu
steps.text: Budi bertanya kepada Rina tentang akhir pekannya.

question.prompt: Lengkapi: Budi: What do you do at the weekend? Rina: On Saturdays I ___ my friends at a café in Bandung.
question.explanation: Untuk orang kita pakai **meet**: **I meet my friends.** **Play** untuk olahraga dan permainan, dan **go** butuh **to** sebelum tempat, bukan sebelum orang.
